function: Radar target detection (number and delay-Doppler location of targets) by a DNN on the OTFS delay-Doppler correlation matrix in an ISAC radar receiver (pp. 2-3).
system: Antennas not stated; single-chain OTFS radar transceiver (Fig. 1, p. 2), no RIS; 24 GHz carrier, 5 MHz bandwidth, M=128, N=64 (p. 5).
method: Supervised DNN: Faster R-CNN with ResNet backbone plus squeeze-and-excitation attention and multi-scale feature fusion, RPN, classification and smooth-L1 regression loss, followed by proposed NMS (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Custom MATLAB simulation: DD-domain point-target channel (eq. 3) with AWGN, 1-6 on-grid targets, random QPSK OTFS frames; 150,000 frames split 1:1:4 into training, validation, test (pp. 2, 5).
test_conditions: Trained only at -5 dB SNR; tested from -5 to 15 dB in 5 dB steps with 1-6 targets, speeds up to 439 km/h (p. 5).
baselines: Classical CA-CFAR detector; learned Faster R-CNN [12] and FCN [13] with ResNet50/ResNet101; ablations without NMS and NMS without quasi-periodicity (p. 5).
metrics: Detection probability (PD) versus false alarm probability (PFA) as ROC curves, PFA versus score gate, and PD versus SNR at fixed PFA (p. 5).
complexity: NMS step only: time O(mn + mn/a^2), space O(mn + NumClusters) (p. 5); no DNN parameters, operations, or runtime reported.
q1_support: p. 2: "where P ∈ Z is the total number of targets in the wireless channel"; p. 5: "We implement the entire experimental simulation data generation and result analysis using MATLAB 2022b." Custom point-target delay-Doppler channel with AWGN; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 5: "we only utilized the train set in −5 dB for training, and the model was tested at different SNRs." This is only an SNR sweep; the 1-6 targets and all other settings are shared by the randomly split training and test sets.
q3_support: p. 5: "comparing it with the CA-CFAR detector, Faster RCNN [12], and FCN [13]." Classical CA-CFAR and learned FCN and Faster R-CNN are compared on detection rate at fixed PFA (Fig. 7(b)).
q4_support: p. 5: "the time complexity is O(mn + mn/a^2), and the space complexity is O(mn + NumClusters)." Order of complexity given for the proposed NMS algorithm; the cost of the DNN itself is not reported.
q5_support: p. 5: "We implement the entire experimental simulation data generation and result analysis using MATLAB 2022b." Self-generated simulated data; no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Eligibility and area are a judgment call. The learned task is radar target detection (sensing), but the system communicates, p. 1: "In our case, as an ISAC system, the radar receiver has knowledge of data information from the transmitter." So the exclusion of sensing alone in a system that does not communicate does not apply. The DNN detects the targets, which are the paths of the delay-Doppler channel (eq. 3, p. 2), so it is read as detection in the DD domain of an OTFS high-mobility link: area 4, which takes precedence over area 5 (the learned method designs no beams, waveforms, or resources). The reviewer may instead judge radar target detection outside the seven functions (exclude: function, p. 1). A single-antenna link is admitted for OTFS works. q3: FCN [13] is an independent standard architecture; Faster R-CNN [12] is the backbone of the proposed network and could be read as an ablation. q4: complexity is reported only for the NMS post-processing, not for the DNN (no parameters, FLOPs, or runtime); the reviewer should confirm whether this suffices.
